issues.description: Test passes a zero-amount addition with zeros puzzle_hash to placate the new validator, masking the real contract
issues.detail: The test changes from `additions=[]` to `[Addition(amount=0, puzzle_hash=zeros)]` to satisfy `CreateSignedTransaction.__post_init__` which requires at least one addition. This complects the CATSpend legacy fallback path (amount/inner_address) with the additions path. The test now exercises a nonsense addition rather than the intended legacy fields. Tests should reflect the actual contract; this is TDD-as-design covering up an incidental conflation.

issues.description: CATSpend legacy fields and additions are complected; the forwarding path silently elides the legacy branch when additions present
issues.detail: CATSpend has two value-shapes (amount+inner_address vs additions). The new `cat_spend` forwarder picks `request.additions if not None else [Addition(amount, decode(inner_address), memos)]`. But callers can pass `additions=[]` (empty list, not None) and bypass the legacy fallback, or pass both. The identity "what coins are being spent" is now ambiguous. Decompose: validate input into one canonical shape before forwarding.

issues.description: `cat_discrepancy_validation` returns a tuple but its inputs are three independent optional fields scattered across two request types
issues.detail: The validator throws when any subset of (extra_delta, tail_reveal, tail_solution) is partially specified. This is essential validation, but the underlying complecting is: three fields on two dataclasses that must move together. Make it a single nested value type (`CatDiscrepancy | None`) on both requests. Then the validator becomes construction, and `None in {...}` checks and `type: ignore` disappear.

issues.description: `send_transaction` discards the wallet object it fetched purely "for the opportunity to raise"
issues.detail: `self.service.wallet_state_manager.get_wallet(...)` is called and its return value thrown away; the comment `# opportunity to raise` admits this. Side-effecting a lookup for validation is place-oriented thinking. Extract a `validate_wallet_id(id, required_type)` function that returns None or raises. The intent becomes simple and the dead binding goes away.

issues.description: `json_serialize_for_transport(...).then call create_signed_transaction` round-trips structured values through JSON for an internal call
issues.detail: Both `send_transaction` and `cat_spend` build a typed `CreateSignedTransaction`, serialize it to JSON, then hand it to `create_signed_transaction` which presumably parses it back. This is incidental complexity from the RPC framework leaking into internal call sites. The value is already a value; pass the value. If `create_signed_transaction` requires JSON, that is the abstraction hiding the data.

issues.description: `CreateSignedTransaction` is accreting unrelated concerns (CAT discrepancy, puzzle_decorator) with a comment admitting the hack
issues.detail: The comment `# Technically this value was meant to support many types here / However, only one is supported right now ... as a slight hack` is honest but is exactly the moment to stop and ask: is `CreateSignedTransaction` the right concept, or are we building a god-request to avoid two simpler endpoints? The deprecation note in the PR description suggests yes — but the right time to think about that is now, not "another time and day".

review.summary: This PR reduces duplication by routing two endpoints through a third — directionally aligned with simplification — but achieves "easy" (less code) rather than "simple" (decomposed concerns). The receiving `CreateSignedTransaction` is now COMPLECTED: it carries XCH-style additions, CAT-specific discrepancy fields, and a puzzle_decorator with an admitted hack. The test change to pass a zero-amount/zero-hash Addition to satisfy `__post_init__` is TDD-AS-DESIGN papering over a contract problem. The question that should have been asked first: do these three endpoints represent one value-shape or three, and if three, why force one dataclass to carry all of them?
